ety.text: Attested since the 16th century; borrowed from Scots wow; ultimately a natural exclamation.

senses.d: An indication of excitement, surprise, astonishment, or pleasure.
ex: Out on thir wanderand spiritis, wow! thow cryis.

senses.d: An expression of amazement, awe, or admiration.
ex: Wow! How do they do that?

senses.d: Used sarcastically to express disapproval of something.
ex: Wow… good job using all of our supplies on the first day.

senses.d: Anything exceptionally surprising, unbelievable, outstanding, etc.
ex: ‘And say, Jimmy, wait till you see me in my new outfit...It’s a wow, kid.’

‘Jesus suffering fuck,’ said Adrian. ‘It’s not half a thought.’
‘Face it, it’s a wow.’
One woman took a seat nearer the front for a closer look at my maps. Several people exhaled loudly. I heard a wow now and then.

senses.d: A relatively slow form of flutter (pitch variation) which can affect both gramophone records and tape recorders.
ex: I often hear flutter and wows spoken of.

fr:waouh.gl: wow (expression of excitement, pleasure, surprise), yay, yippie; yahoo

it:per tutti i diavoli.gl: wow (an indication of excitement or surprise)

pt:nossa.gl: oh, my God!; goodness! (said in excitement, shock, awe or dismay)

ety.text: Shortening of nossa senhora (literally “our lady”), itself a shortening of minha nossa senhora (literally “my our lady”). The expression minha nossa senhora is probably influenced by meu Deus (literally “my God”), similarly to English Oh, my God and Spanish Dios mío.

es:guau.gl: woof, bow wow (the sound a dog makes when barking)

ety.text: Univerbation of hijo (“son”) + le (pronoun), an ellipsis of hijo de puta or similar expressions.
